title: CI runs pytest without installing it in a repo that has Python tests and no backend
symptom: The first GitHub Actions run (workflow run 44650279227) failed with `python: No module named pytest`. verify.py runs pytest for every web repo, but .github/workflows/ci.yml installs Python dependencies only when backend/requirements.txt exists. client-portal has Python tests at shared/auth/test_auth.py and shared/db/test_db.py and no backend/ directory, so nothing was ever installed. The local run passed only because pytest is installed machine-wide.
reproduce: a clean ubuntu-latest runner with Python 3.11 has no pytest
expected: A repo that runs pytest installs pytest, whether or not it has a backend directory.
fix_commit: working tree (uncommitted); the CI workflow installs pytest whenever Python tests exist
regression_test: the ci workflow itself on a clean runner
root_cause: The scaffold CI template treated Python as an optional backend concern and gated the whole install on backend/requirements.txt, while verify.py treats pytest as a standard step for every web repo. The two disagreed, and only a clean runner exposed it: the local machine already had pytest.
bench_note: A committed failing state, a small workflow fix and a CI run that decides pass or fail.
notes: Scaffold-level defect: the same template is vendored into docs-answer and triage-agent, which pass only because they do have a backend. The template needs the same correction so the next repo does not repeat it.
